bib.title: Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Scaling Laws for Agent Harnesses via Effective Feedback Compute", Xuanliang Zhang, Dingzirui Wang, Keyan Xu, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che (corresponding), Harbin Institute of Technology. arXiv 2605.29682v2 [cs.CL], 24 Jun 2026. Preprint (no venue printed; ACL-style format).

COVERAGE: All 29 pages, 109,131 chars, read in full: main text, references, appendices A-F, and the per-model figures 13-33. I only skimmed the numeric axis tick lines of the plot extractions. There is no limitations section (a search for "Limitation" found nothing).

CORE CLAIM: Raw test-time spend (tokens, tool calls, wall time, cost) does not predict harness success. "Effective Feedback Compute" (EFC) does. EFC counts feedback events by informativeness x validity x non-redundancy x retention (Eq 4: EFC_t = kappa*I*V*R*M, kappa=10). Normalised by task demand D_task, it fits failure rate far better. The paper also proposes EFC-Adapter, a companion layer that ranks, retains, and stops feedback actions by EFC per unit raw cost.

FUNCTIONAL FORM: Power law on failure rate, E(z) = E_inf + A*z^(-alpha) (Eq 15), where z is a median-normalised scalar predictor. D_task = max{eps, L*H_tool*S_state*(1+N_obs)*(1-V_ver)} (Eq 12). Harness efficiency eta = EFC/C_raw.

HEADLINE NUMBERS (all averaged over 3 small models: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, gpt-5.4-nano, Claude-Haiku-4.5; the number of runs and tasks is not stated)
- Controlled synthetic tasks (Needle Lookup, State Tracking, Rule Filter): R2 is 0.99 for Oracle-EFC/D_task, 0.95 for Oracle-EFC and Estimated-EFC, 0.68 for SAS, and 0.27 for raw tokens (best raw), 0.01 for raw cost. Fig 1, p.4.
- Matched budget (raw-cost delta 0.000%, tool-call delta 0): success rises from 0.27 to 0.90 (p<1e-6) when only feedback quality changes. Fig 2.
- Real traces (HumanEval, Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, pooled): NRS-EFC/D_task R2 = 0.93, NRS-EFC 0.89, SAS 0.44, raw baselines -0.02 to -0.08. Fig 8.
- Prospective holdout, with the protocol frozen first: R2 = 0.89 (NRS-EFC/D_task), 0.82 (NRS-EFC), 0.28 (SAS), raw negative. Fig 9.
- EFC-Adapter on mini-SWE-agent, AHE, RTV and PDR, across the 3 models: mean pass rate 61.2% -> 68.2%, mean raw cost 213.8 -> 85.1, with the same model, tools and budget caps. Fig 10.

ABLATIONS
- Fig 4 (high minus low effect on eta): router quality +0.28, verifier strength +0.22, memory fidelity +0.20; observation noise -0.17, tool entropy -0.11, state pressure -0.05.
- Fig 12 (module ablations): mean eta explains success with R2 = 0.97, raw cost with R2 = 0.01.
- H4 "High Budget Noisy" is a negative control. It spends more with weak verification and memory, and its success is poor.
- The verifier is one of several factors, and it is not tested as stronger than the executor.

SLICE RESULTS (Sec 6.2)
- On HumanEval, H5/H6 (closed loop) give the highest eta.
- On Terminal-Bench, all harnesses have low eta.
- On SWE-bench, the simple H0 and H3 are strongest and H5/H6 no longer dominate.

QUOTES
- "Matched-budget interventions further show that improving feedback quality raises success from 0.27 to 0.90 without changing raw cost or tool calls." (p.1)
- "These reversals suggest that η reflects a harness–task interaction rather than an invariant property of the harness alone." (p.7)
- "mean η explains almost all variation in success (R2 = 0.97), whereas raw cost explains almost none (R2 = 0.01)." (App E.2, p.17)
- "the fitted denominator should be read as a distribution-specific calibration of Dtask, not as a universal causal weighting." (p.6)

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN
- The core evidence is synthetic. Appendix D.3.9 says controlled experiments use "explicit simulation parameters", so H0-H6 are partly simulated roles, not real agent implementations.
- On real benchmarks, Estimated-EFC uses hand-set gates and constants. The status-quality weights Q_t and gate values are chosen by the authors.
- Per-benchmark pass rates, n of tasks, number of repeated runs and dollar costs are not given. "Cost" is a synthetic weighted unit (Eq 33).
- The R2 values come from fits of 2-3 parameters to aggregated group failure rates, so they say little about per-task prediction.
- There is no test of a stronger-than-executor verifier, of generation versus evaluation separation, of retry taxonomy, or of reasoning-token budgets. There is no "delete the verifier" experiment.
- The models are small and cheap. EFC-Adapter helps weaker models most.
- Only a small prospective holdout was run. No code release is mentioned. Adapter gains are not broken out by task, and no ablation of Adapter parts is shown.
- The authors concede the matched-budget comparison "does not rule out all differences between trajectory types". Verifier visibility V_ver is part of the demand term.

BUILDS ON: Kaplan et al. 2020 and Hoffmann et al. 2022 (scaling laws); Snell et al. 2025 (test-time compute); Brown et al. 2025 (repeated sampling); Kim et al. 2026b "Towards a science of scaling agent systems" (SAS baseline); Kim et al. 2026a (RTV/PDR test-time scaling); Yang et al. 2024 (SWE-agent / mini-SWE-agent); Lin et al. 2026 (AHE); Liu et al. 2025 (budget-aware tool use); ReAct (Yao 2023); Reflexion (Shinn 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan 2023); Lightman 2024 (verify step by step).

FIT TO NOTES: Weak and indirect for 05-verification-loops. It gives only generic support: verifier strength is one of the top-3 efficiency levers (+0.22, Fig 4), and extra loops with flat marginal feedback should stop (Eq 37). It does not address asymmetric QA, deletion of a verifier, retry taxonomy or reasoning budgets. A better fit is 02-harness-anatomy (routing, verification and memory as the three conversion modules), or a measuring-harness-effectiveness or cost-efficiency section if one exists. I would file it as a "sharpens" citation with caution: the evidence is largely synthetic, and I read nothing that would justify a strong claim.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Fig 12 (p.17), "Module ablations localize raw-to-EFC conversion gains". Right panel: success vs eta R2=0.97, vs raw cost R2=0.01. Alternative: Fig 2 (p.4), the matched-budget bar chart 0.27 -> 0.90.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions were found. Equations and figure text extracted garbled but were readable. Use quotes with care because line breaks are mid-sentence.
